## Summary

Magneti Marelli began in 1919 as a joint venture of Fiat and Ercole Marelli, was a Fiat subsidiary from 1967, was the subject of a sale by FCA to KKR announced in 2018 and merged with Calsonic Kansei in May 2019 to form Marelli, headquartered in Corbetta, Italy [3]. Its Guangzhou electronics plant, established in 1996 as Marelli's first manufacturing site in China, employs nearly 1,000 people on 66 production lines and builds digital cockpits, digital instrument clusters, 5G telematics systems, body and seat ECUs, zone control units and Mini-LED and MicroLED displays for customers in and outside China [2]. The IEEE registry lists one MA-L block to this entity at Jinghu Road, Guangzhou [1].

A MAC in this block is most likely a vehicle's cockpit, cluster or telematics unit built in Guangzhou, so the brand on the car is the automaker, not Marelli [2]. Marelli's ProConnect platform for the China market runs cluster, infotainment and 5G Release 15 telematics on one MediaTek MT8675 SoC, though the release does not say which plant builds it [4]. FCC grantee codes, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth radios, randomization and security advisories are not documented for this entity by the sources consulted [2][4].
